notes: Phase 3 Commit D of the [2026-08-11 non-Enterprise session cleanup plan](vault/artifacts/2026-08-11-non-enterprise-session-cleanup-plan.md) — audit surgery. Retires all vendor-transcript-discovery code paths from `gator-audit.py::assemble_audit_data()`, unblocking the whole-file deletes in Commit E. Ordering matters: doing file deletes first would break the snippet-reader path (spurious `if sessions_mod:` guard also wrapped `sessions_dirs` gathering).

Deleted `_committed_decisions_from_raw_vendor_logs()` fn (~70 lines, extracted in Phase 2B for exactly this deletion). Deleted the `elif common:` dispatch site in `assemble_audit_data()` (7 lines). Behavior: `data["decisions_source"]` is now always `"committed"` when any summaries exist; no `"raw-vendor-logs"` value survives.

Deleted the "Sessions — filtered to fleet repos only" block (~65 lines): `sessions_mod = _import_script("gator-sessions")` init, the outer `if sessions_mod:` guard, all `sessions_mod.discover_all_sessions/parse_since/filter_sessions_since/get_pending_sessions` call sites, and the `data["sessions"] = {by_vendor, by_repo, pending_export, total, exported, recent}` assembly. Per parent plan §5 decision 4 = (i) drop vendor-derived fields silently: `data["sessions"]` stays as the `{}` init from the top of the function; dashboard consumers (`audit.js:258/274/335/343`) default defensively (`sessions.by_vendor || {}` etc.), so empty tiles are the accepted honest degrade.

Restructured the decisions section: removed the spurious outer `if sessions_mod:` guard around `sessions_dirs` gathering (gathering only uses `find_command_post` + `parse_registry` + `normalize_path` + `gator_remote` — none from `sessions_mod`). Un-indented the block by one level. Removed the "prefer committed / fall back to vendor logs" comment prose (no fallback remains). `assemble_audit_data()` shrunk from ~380 lines to ~230.

`common = _import_script("gator-session-common")` init preserved — still used at L355 for `data["machine"] = common.get_machine_identity()`. Commit F retargets that call to `reader_mod.get_machine_identity()` after folding the helper into `gator_session_reader.py`, then removes the `common` import from audit.py.

Charter updates: `.gator/charters/scripts-fleet-intelligence.md` — `assemble_audit_data()` entry rewritten (no vendor mention, sessions-empty tripwire added, `->` list pruned); the `_committed_decisions_from_raw_vendor_logs` entry replaced with a one-line retirement stub for reader continuity. `.gator/charters/scripts-cross-cutting.md` — `gator-audit.py` degradation bullet updated to reflect the reduced optional-module set (5 → 4) and the vendor-branch retirement.

Verification: full test suite **867 passed, 2 xfailed** (pre-existing v2.6.0 xfails). Zero regressions. `tests/test_audit_integration.py` (3 tests) exercises `assemble_audit_data` end-to-end — snippet-reader path still produces `decisions_source: "committed"` with the expected decisions extracted from fleet repos.

Significance-check assessment (constitution step 7): touches no public CLI verb (`--sessions` mode continues via a separate code path — `_handle_sessions()` — that uses `gator-session-aggregator`, unaffected). No cross-module TRIPWIRE violated: the `parse_committed_summary` canonical parser TRIPWIRE (r2 updated) now has exactly one owner (`gator_session_reader.py`) after this commit, since the last vendor-side consumer (`gator-audit.py`'s DELETE-VENDOR helper) is gone. No security-relevant code. Steelman argument against: the `data["sessions"]: {}` silent-empty is a soft behavior change — the Audit dashboard's "Sessions by agent" / "Sessions by repo" tiles now render empty. Response: this is the exact behavior the Architect ratified as (i) at Phase 3 kickoff; the field's semantics ("counts across raw vendor transcripts on the machine") have no snippet-based equivalent, and inventing one for cosmetic UI reasons is out of scope per parent plan §5 decision 4.
